pathway.title: Qnity Electronics, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The business is the main strength: consumable materials qualified into customer roadmaps drove nine-month net sales growth of 20.65%, all of it volume with price and mix flat, and lifted gross margin by 0.96 percentage points to 47.14%. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation FC2; calculation FC3; calculation FC19

- Operating leverage is working for creditors so far: Adjusted Operating EBITDA rose USD 254 million on USD 736 million of extra net sales, an incremental margin of 34.51% against an average of 31.28%, although selling, general and administrative costs grew 26.49%, faster than sales. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation FC3; calculation FC4

- Leverage is moderate and earnings-led: total debt was 2.72x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 2.87x at 2025-12-31 and net debt 1.96x against 2.22x, with debt almost unchanged, so the cushion holds only while earnings do; pro forma net leverage after the dividend declared on 2026-10-14 is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation FC1; calculation FC16

- Cash conversion is the weak spot: free cash flow was 31.23% of reported EBITDA in the nine months against 53.23% a year earlier because interest costs on the separation debt rose, working capital absorbed USD 134 million and capital expenditures rose, so the improvement in leverage has not yet become cash. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation FC6; calculation FC7; calculation FC8

- Liquidity and maturities leave no near-term refinancing pressure, but the debt is back-ended and largely floating: 97.07% of principal falls due in 2032 and 2033, 57.19% of principal bears a floating rate, and each 100 bp costs about USD 24 million a year. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation FC13; calculation FC14

- Concentration is the primary downside path: the top ten customers took 34% of 2025 sales with no purchase commitments, Samsung and TSMC took 10% each in the nine months of 2026, and Asia Pacific supplied 78.82% of 2025 sales, so one export-control, tariff or inventory shock reaches most of the volume at once. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation FC18; calculation FC20

- Governance is a moderate constraint: sponsor and governance risk is Medium because DuPont controls legacy liabilities of USD 218 million, 14.74% of reported EBITDA, and shareholder returns took 35.01% of nine-month free cash flow. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation FC18

- Management guidance is strong but implies a pause: it was raised at each of the last three releases to net sales of USD 5,770 million to USD 5,830 million, yet it implies fourth-quarter Adjusted Operating EBITDA 10.54% below the third quarter at the midpoint. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-12_exhibit991supplementalsche.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-04_exhibit991supplementalsche.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_exhibit991supplementalsche.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation FC11; calculation FC12

runs.text: The five strongest credit supports, in order, are these. First, consumable materials qualified into customer roadmaps give recurring volume, which lifted nine-month net sales 20.65% and supports debt service for as long as customers keep producing. Second, margins widened with volume, with gross margin up 0.96 percentage points and an incremental Adjusted Operating EBITDA margin of 34.51%, which lets earnings outgrow debt. Third, leverage is moderate at 2.72x reported EBITDA and liquidity of USD 2,362 million covers twelve-month debt service 9.12x. Fourth, 97.07% of principal falls due in 2032 and 2033, so no refinancing is needed before the revolver matures in October 2030. Fifth, about 70% of raw materials are sourced locally and no supplier exceeds 10% of raw material spend, which limits input and tariff shocks. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation FC1; calculation FC2; calculation FC4; calculation FC14; calculation FC19

The five largest credit weaknesses, in order, are these. First, the top ten customers took 34% of 2025 sales without purchase commitments and Asia Pacific supplied 78.82%, so one shock hits most volume. Second, free cash flow conversion fell to 31.23% from 53.23% as working capital absorbed USD 134 million, and the reported-to-adjusted EBITDA gap of USD 216 million means cash costs sit outside the adjusted measure. Third, DuPont controls legacy liabilities of USD 218 million that Qnity must fund, with up to about USD 100 million more reasonably possible. Fourth, 57.19% of principal floats and no hedge is disclosed, so each 100 bp costs about USD 24 million a year, and cash paid for interest is not stated in any filing. Fifth, buybacks and dividends took 35.01% of nine-month free cash flow with the limits of the executed documents not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation FC1; calculation FC6; calculation FC7; calculation FC13; calculation FC18

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The separation was a spin-off and not a sponsor transaction: DuPont announced the plan on 2024-05-22 and completed it on 2025-11-01 by distributing one Qnity share for every two DuPont shares, and Qnity common stock began trading on the New York Stock Exchange on 2025-11-03. No acquirer, purchase price, equity contribution or entry multiple exists, and the sources and uses of the separation are not stated beyond the debt below. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8

Qnity borrowed USD 4,100 million before the distribution: USD 1,000 million of secured notes due 2032 and USD 750 million of unsecured notes due 2033 issued on 2025-08-15, and a USD 2,350 million term loan due 2032 funded on 2025-10-31, with the term loan and the notes proceeds paid to DuPont as a cash dividend. The secured debt is 81.71% of the total, and a USD 1,250 million revolver maturing in October 2030, undrawn at 2026-09-30, adds committed capacity under a first lien net leverage test of 4.50x. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation BG7

On 2026-07-01 the term loan was repriced: the margin fell by 25 bp to 1.75% over term SOFR, USD 360 million of principal was repaid and reissued and the rest rolled over, and the issuer expects annual cash interest to fall by about USD 6 million. Both series of notes can be redeemed before 2028-08-15 only at par plus a make-whole premium, or in part from equity offerings. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117; calculation BG8

No new debt issuance is stated in the nine months to 2026-09-30: the only change to debt terms was the repricing, and cash went to buybacks of USD 75 million and dividends of USD 50 million in nine months. Legacy payments to DuPont are not debt but are claims outside it, at USD 218 million accrued, and the executed documents that fix distribution and lien capacity were not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation BG9; calculation BG10

fields.value: Qnity Electronics, Inc. (issuer q), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the financial foundation of the issuer's consolidated statements, debt, liquidity and credit ratios, built from the FY2025 annual report, the three 2026 quarterly reports and the three 2026 results releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Qnity's leverage is moderate and falling: total debt was 2.72x and net debt 1.96x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, against 2.87x and 2.22x at 2025-12-31, and scheduled maturities are only USD 24 million a year through 2030. Cash interest paid is not stated in any filing, so cash interest cover is not established; reported EBITDA covered nine-month interest expense of USD 186 million 6.15x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage fell between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30 because earnings grew while debt barely moved. Carrying-value debt was USD 4,027 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 4,019 million at 2026-09-30, after USD 18 million of term loan installments in nine months, so total debt to reported EBITDA fell from 2.87x to 2.72x almost wholly because last-twelve-month reported EBITDA rose from USD 1,403 million to USD 1,479 million. Net debt to reported EBITDA fell further, from 2.22x to 1.96x, because cash rose from USD 915 million to USD 1,124 million. For creditors this means the improvement so far is earnings-led rather than repayment-led, so it holds only while EBITDA holds.

Contractual interest due within the next twelve months is USD 236 million, which last-twelve-month reported EBITDA of USD 1,479 million covers 6.27x. fields.value: Free cash flow, operating cash flow less capital expenditures, fell to USD 357 million in the nine months of 2026 from USD 568 million a year earlier, and conversion of reported EBITDA fell from 53.23% to 31.23%. Operating cash flow fell by USD 135 million to USD 647 million and capital expenditures rose by USD 76 million to USD 290 million; the issuer attributes the lower operating cash flow to interest payments on debt that was not outstanding a year earlier and to working capital, where receivables absorbed USD 230 million and inventories USD 107 million against a USD 203 million rise in payables. Sales growth of 20.65% drove the working capital build, so the earnings-led deleveraging has not yet converted into cash at the same rate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 6, 42; calculation F21; calculation F23

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer's Adjusted Free Cash Flow of USD 607 million for the nine months is USD 250 million above the method figure because it adds back transformation charges of USD 84 million, indirect legacy costs of USD 114 million and a separation foreign tax cost of USD 52 million. Those are cash outflows that fund the separation and DuPont indemnities, so the method figure is the one that measures cash available to creditors, and the guidance for FY2026 adjusted free cash flow of USD 800 million to USD 900 million is on the issuer definition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is USD 2,362 million, cash of USD 1,124 million plus USD 1,238 million of undrawn revolver after USD 12 million of letters of credit, which is 0.59x total debt and covers the USD 259 million of principal and interest due within twelve months 9.12x. Two limits qualify it: USD 785 million of the cash is held by foreign subsidiaries, and the revolver carries a first lien net leverage test of 4.50:1.00 for which the issuer states compliance but not the ratio, so no covenant headroom is worked here. Uncommitted lines of about USD 136 million add flexibility but are not committed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 19, 20, 21, 41, 43; calculation F17; calculation F28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scheduled maturities are term loan installments of USD 24 million a year from FY2026 to FY2030, with USD 3,980 million falling due afterwards, led by the 2032 secured notes, the 2032 term loan balance and the 2033 unsecured notes; the revolver matures in October 2030 and is undrawn. Outside the debt figure sit operating lease liabilities of USD 514 million, pension and other post-employment liabilities of USD 81 million and DuPont indemnification liabilities of USD 81 million current and USD 137 million noncurrent for legacy matters, with a further exposure reasonably possible of about USD 100 million; the documents give a second, larger indemnification total at 2025-12-31, so the claim is bounded by definition rather than by one figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2025 comparatives are a DuPont carve-out until 2025-11-01 and the releases state their headline prior-period figures on a pro forma basis, so a growth rate or margin trend that mixes reported and pro forma figures would mislead; every comparison here names its basis. The 2026-07-01 repricing is a multi-figure event: about USD 1,978 million of the term loan rolled over without cash, about USD 360 million was repaid and reissued (a gross cash inflow and outflow that net to nil), and the cost was USD 3 million of loss on extinguishment in interest expense and USD 2 million of fees in other expense, with a 1.00% premium on repricing events for six months; the margin cut is expected to save about USD 6 million of annual cash interest. No customer deposits or supplier finance programs are disclosed and deferred revenue is USD 47 million at 2025-12-31, so no non-debt funding float is flagged. The dividend declared on 2026-10-14 is a subsequent event kept out of the 2026-09-30 figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The most material gap is cash paid for interest, which no filing states: without it the method's cash interest cover cannot be calculated and creditors rely on an expense ratio of 6.15x and a contractual ratio of 6.27x. The second is the unreconciled indemnification totals, which leave claims outside debt as a range, from USD 81 million current and USD 137 million noncurrent legacy liabilities to a larger total at the 2025-12-31 definition. The third is the missing term loan principal and unamortized costs at 2026-09-30, which confines the principal-to-carrying reconciliation to 2025-12-31.

fields.value: Each row shows the inputs and the result; amounts are USD millions unless stated. Figures taken directly from a filing are in the statement tables, and the rows below are what this module worked out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash paid for interest is printed as a dash in the 2025 annual report for FY2023 to FY2025 and is absent from the 2026 quarterly reports, so the Cash Interest Paid row and every cash interest cover ratio are not supplied for all periods; this restricts the method's coverage measure and is a High severity gap; the action that would close it is the company's cash paid for interest, or the next annual report's supplemental cash flow note.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Term loan principal and unamortized discount and issuance costs at 2026-09-30 are not printed, because the quarterly report refers to the annual report for the tranche table and states contractual principal only as about USD 4.1 billion; this confines the debt principal reconciliation and the maturity ladder to 2025-12-31 and is a Medium severity gap; the action is the next annual report's debt note.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The DuPont indemnification totals differ by definition: liabilities for future payments due to DuPont of USD 461 million at 2025-12-31 against legacy liabilities of USD 190 million recorded in the contingencies note, and the 2026-09-30 report prints only the legacy figures of USD 81 million and USD 137 million and a current line of USD 155 million; this limits the size of claims outside debt and is a Medium severity gap; the action is to confirm the definitions with the company.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No balance sheet at 2023-12-31 or 2025-09-30 is printed in the sources, so debt, cash and leverage are not supplied for those dates and the leverage history starts at 2024-12-31; this is a Low severity gap; the action is the FY2024 annual report or the Q3 2025 quarterly report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Instrument-level carrying values are not disclosed, only principal and one aggregate financing cost of USD 73 million at 2025-12-31, and the seniority split of balance-sheet debt is therefore built from principal; this is a Low severity gap; the action is the executed debt documents or a note with carrying values.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2025 comparatives are carve-out statements and the releases state their headline prior-period figures on a pro forma basis, with Adjusted Operating EBITDA for Q3 2025 at USD 382 million as reported and USD 370 million pro forma; this limits growth and margin comparisons and is a Medium severity gap; the action is to label every comparison by basis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Printed dashes are carried as nil for interest expense in FY2023 and FY2024, for the debt lines at 2024-12-31 and for cash flow lines a statement omits, because the totals tie without them and the annual report states zero debt at 2024-12-31; this is an interpretation rather than a stated zero and is a Low severity gap; the action is to confirm with the filing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash taxes paid are not supplied for the nine months of 2025 and 2026 because the quarterly reports print no supplemental cash flow information; this is a Low severity gap; the action is the next annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The margin now applied to the revolver within its range of 1.25% to 2.25% over term SOFR is not stated, so the spread of that facility is not supplied; this is a Low severity gap; the action is the compliance certificate or the executed credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The cash amount of the dividend declared on 2026-10-14 is not stated, so the pro forma net debt and net leverage after it are not supplied; this is a Low severity gap; the action is the record-date share count after 2026-11-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Undrawn committed facilities at 2024-12-31 are not supplied because the revolver was entered on 2025-10-31 and no earlier committed facility is stated; this is a Low severity gap; no action is needed beyond reading the FY2024 row as pre-separation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Maintenance and growth capital expenditures are not split, so only total capital expenditures are carried; this is a Low severity gap; the action is management disclosure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Operating measures such as volumes are stated only as percentage changes of net sales, so no period-end or flow operating rows are carried; this is a Low severity gap; the action is management disclosure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The first lien net leverage ratio the issuer reports against its 4.50:1.00 revolver test is not stated, so covenant headroom is not worked; this is a Medium severity gap owned by Legal & covenants; the action is the compliance certificate and the executed credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership is public and sponsor-free on the evidence supplied, but control is not fully dispersed: one preferred share held by a trust must consent to charter changes that protect DuPont authority over legacy claims, so creditors cannot count on the board to contest DuPont decisions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The separation put USD 4,100 million of debt on Qnity and sent the proceeds to DuPont as a cash dividend, the one documented extraction-type action, and nothing creditor-adverse is documented in the supplied documents since: the 2026-07-01 repricing cut the term loan margin by 25 bp, with USD 360 million repaid and reissued and no change to principal, maturity or covenants.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation BG7; calculation BG8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Legacy liabilities to DuPont are the exposure outside reported debt that governance matters most for, because DuPont and not Qnity controls it: USD 218 million was accrued at 2026-09-30 against USD 190 million at 2025-12-31, up to about USD 100 million more is reasonably possible, USD 74 million of allocated payments fell due in the third quarter of 2026, and DuPont alone decides settlements while Qnity pays 44%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Shareholder returns are moderate so far but discretionary: buybacks of USD 75 million and dividends of USD 50 million took 35.01% of nine-month free cash flow, USD 425 million of the USD 500 million authorization remains, and the credit agreement and indentures that would limit this were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation BG9; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance is adequate but still transitional: the board of ten has a separate Chair and the auditor gave an unmodified opinion with one critical audit matter on revenue recognition, but finance leadership was interim into 2026, Qnity relied on DuPont for controls until 2025-11-01, and it began exiting transition services only in the third quarter of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Related-party funding outside debt is small but growing: the note payable to a nonconsolidated affiliate rose to USD 100 million from USD 53 million at 2025-12-31 and USD 31 million a year earlier, equal to 11.29% of accounts payable, and sits in accounts payable rather than in debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a lower level is that no sponsor extracts value, the franchise is growing on volume, and the legacy liabilities are small against earnings: the accrued USD 218 million is 14.74% of last-twelve-month reported EBITDA, and 21.50% if the reasonably possible range is added. Management has raised full-year guidance at each of the last three results releases, and most lenders rolled their term loan balances, 84.60% of the repriced principal, when the margin was cut.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Against that, the level is Medium rather than Low because the one documented value transfer was large, DuPont and the trust hold rights that creditors cannot contest, and customer and regional concentration leave sales exposed to one large customer decision or one export-control change.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The level would rise to High if executed documents show restricted-payment baskets that allow materially larger distributions, if Qnity adds debt for an acquisition or a special dividend, or if DuPont settlements lift the accrual well beyond the reasonably possible range. It would fall to Low if the proxy statement confirms dispersed ownership with no holder above 5%, if the legacy indemnities end or are capped, and if indenture terms limit distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement that carries holders above 5%, director holdings and board independence was not supplied, so the finding that no controlling holder exists could be overturned by a large holder and would then raise the governance level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement, its first amendment and both indentures were not supplied, so the finding that shareholder returns are moderate rests on observed behavior and not on legal capacity; larger restricted-payment baskets would move the level toward High.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Legacy liability sizing rests on DuPont estimates that Qnity does not control, so the USD 218 million accrual and the reasonably possible range of about USD 100 million are the least firm inputs to the Medium level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue is disclosed by segment, region and the top two customers only, so the finding that concentration is customer and regional rather than product-level cannot be tested for individual product lines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No ratings, market prices or executed customer contracts were supplied, so the view that demand is recurring rests on the company description of long customer relationships.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The separation was a spin-off and not a sponsor transaction: DuPont announced the plan on 2024-05-22 and completed it on 2025-11-01 by distributing one Qnity share for every two DuPont shares, and Qnity common stock began trading on the New York Stock Exchange on 2025-11-03. No acquirer, purchase price, equity contribution or entry multiple exists, and the sources and uses of the separation are not stated beyond the debt below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Qnity borrowed USD 4,100 million before the distribution: USD 1,000 million of secured notes due 2032 and USD 750 million of unsecured notes due 2033 issued on 2025-08-15, and a USD 2,350 million term loan due 2032 funded on 2025-10-31, with the term loan and the notes proceeds paid to DuPont as a cash dividend. The secured debt is 81.71% of the total, and a USD 1,250 million revolver maturing in October 2030, undrawn at 2026-09-30, adds committed capacity under a first lien net leverage test of 4.50x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-07-01 the term loan was repriced: the margin fell by 25 bp to 1.75% over term SOFR, USD 360 million of principal was repaid and reissued and the rest rolled over, and the issuer expects annual cash interest to fall by about USD 6 million. Both series of notes can be redeemed before 2028-08-15 only at par plus a make-whole premium, or in part from equity offerings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new debt issuance is stated in the nine months to 2026-09-30: the only change to debt terms was the repricing, and cash went to buybacks of USD 75 million and dividends of USD 50 million in nine months. Legacy payments to DuPont are not debt but are claims outside it, at USD 218 million accrued, and the executed documents that fix distribution and lien capacity were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: ready with limitations, because ownership percentages, the executed debt documents and the proxy statement are not in the source set.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Qnity presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behavior is the debt-funded cash dividend of USD 4,100 million of borrowed principal to DuPont at the separation, which matters because it left Qnity with the debt and with uncapped legacy indemnities that DuPont controls, and implies cash calls outside debt service that Qnity cannot contest. Countervailing evidence is the absence of any sponsor, the volume-led growth, the repricing without covenant change and shareholder returns of 35.01% of free cash flow. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit agreement and indentures, and DuPont estimates for the legacy liabilities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Beneficial ownership above 5%, holdings of directors and officers, board independence and committee detail are in a proxy statement that was not supplied; this matters because it decides whether any holder or group can control votes or act as a sponsor, and the finding of no sponsor rests on absence; it is a Material severity gap and the action is to obtain the 2026 proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement, its first amendment and both indentures were not supplied; only the summaries in the annual and quarterly reports are available; this matters because capacity to distribute cash, add secured debt or prime creditors cannot be separated from observed behavior; it is a Material severity gap and the action is to obtain executed credit agreement, first amendment and indentures filed as exhibits.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The cash dividend to DuPont at the separation is not separated from ordinary net transfers to DuPont of USD 4,229 million in 2025; the filings state that the full term loan and the notes proceeds were paid to DuPont, and debt issuance costs were USD 88 million; this matters because it sizes the value transfer to the former parent; it is a Minor severity gap and the action is to obtain separation-date sources and uses statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue by line of business, product family and end market is not disclosed and customers beyond the top two are not named; this matters because product and customer concentration beyond the top ten cannot be tested; it is a Minor severity gap and the action is to obtain management disclosure or investor presentation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No sponsor, fund vintage, fund life, fees, equity contribution, purchase price or entry multiple is stated because none applies on the evidence; this matters because sponsor willingness and exit pressure cannot be assessed and are not inferred; it is a Minor severity gap and the action is to obtain the 2026 proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The size of legacy exposures rests on DuPont estimates and the filings say further costs beyond the reasonably possible range cannot be estimated; this matters because it limits the sizing of claims outside debt; it is a Minor severity gap and the action is to obtain duPont disclosures and Qnity notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The permanent Chief Financial Officer is not named in the supplied pages after the interim period; this matters because it bears on leadership continuity through the stand-alone build; it is a Minor severity gap and the action is to obtain current report on Form 8-K or proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Compliance certificates and the actual first lien net leverage ratio are not supplied; this matters because headroom against the first lien net leverage test is not established here; it is a Minor severity gap and the action is to obtain compliance certificate or the executed credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Terms of the Series A Preferred Stock certificate of designation and trust agreement are not supplied; this matters because the extent of entrenchment is read from risk-factor summaries only; it is a Minor severity gap and the action is to obtain certificate of designation and trust agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Remaining term and cost of the transition services agreements and the stand-alone information technology spend to date are not stated; this matters because it bears on dependence on DuPont and on one-time cash costs; it is a Minor severity gap and the action is to obtain management disclosure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The subsidiaries with noncontrolling interests and their holders are not named, and the names of the two other nonconsolidated affiliates and the 2026-09-30 ownership percentages are not stated; this matters because it bears on structural claims and the cash-pooling exposure; it is a Minor severity gap and the action is to obtain annual report subsidiaries exhibit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit ratings, market prices for the notes or analyst views are supplied; this matters because there is no external check on the Medium level; it is a Minor severity gap and the action is to obtain rating agency reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Qnity Electronics, Inc. (issuer q), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the integrated fundamental credit synthesis of the issuer, built from the FY2025 annual report, the three 2026 quarterly reports, the three 2026 results releases and the three earlier modules.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three handoffs were supplied: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 47c46802ce50c3baf8eabe73477d01eed2b624f89e45e6e1ee3e3ba8b02155b0; Financial foundation (CP-1), sha256 12587b6f54163125bf5f71f073b5e8f9637ea2b79b8c75b3dce1be2248fdc921; Business & governance (CP-1A), sha256 63df62730a0ff567a28828eca6acc4463439d42f7eae467c82deb130b4af4fe7. The run settings are not listed as a source.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Qnity's fundamental credit profile is solid and improving: volume-led growth, a 30.87% adjusted EBITDA margin and total leverage of 2.72x reported EBITDA leave creditors a cushion, but dependence on a few Asian customers and cash conversion that fell in 2026 are the main threats. Liquidity of USD 2,362 million covers principal and interest due within twelve months 9.12x, and 97.07% of principal falls due in 2032 and 2033.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; calculation FC1; calculation FC14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside is an export-control, tariff or customer-inventory shock to the 78.82% of sales earned in Asia Pacific, where customers can cancel orders, semi-fixed costs would deleverage margins, and legacy payments to DuPont and shareholder returns would continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation FC3; calculation FC18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business is the main strength: consumable materials qualified into customer roadmaps drove nine-month net sales growth of 20.65%, all of it volume with price and mix flat, and lifted gross margin by 0.96 percentage points to 47.14%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation FC2; calculation FC3; calculation FC19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Operating leverage is working for creditors so far: Adjusted Operating EBITDA rose USD 254 million on USD 736 million of extra net sales, an incremental margin of 34.51% against an average of 31.28%, although selling, general and administrative costs grew 26.49%, faster than sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation FC3; calculation FC4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is moderate and earnings-led: total debt was 2.72x last-twelve-month reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 2.87x at 2025-12-31 and net debt 1.96x against 2.22x, with debt almost unchanged, so the cushion holds only while earnings do; pro forma net leverage after the dividend declared on 2026-10-14 is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation FC1; calculation FC16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash conversion is the weak spot: free cash flow was 31.23% of reported EBITDA in the nine months against 53.23% a year earlier because interest costs on the separation debt rose, working capital absorbed USD 134 million and capital expenditures rose, so the improvement in leverage has not yet become cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation FC6; calculation FC7; calculation FC8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity and maturities leave no near-term refinancing pressure, but the debt is back-ended and largely floating: 97.07% of principal falls due in 2032 and 2033, 57.19% of principal bears a floating rate, and each 100 bp costs about USD 24 million a year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation FC13; calculation FC14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Concentration is the primary downside path: the top ten customers took 34% of 2025 sales with no purchase commitments, Samsung and TSMC took 10% each in the nine months of 2026, and Asia Pacific supplied 78.82% of 2025 sales, so one export-control, tariff or inventory shock reaches most of the volume at once.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation FC18; calculation FC20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance is a moderate constraint: sponsor and governance risk is Medium because DuPont controls legacy liabilities of USD 218 million, 14.74% of reported EBITDA, and shareholder returns took 35.01% of nine-month free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management guidance is strong but implies a pause: it was raised at each of the last three releases to net sales of USD 5,770 million to USD 5,830 million, yet it implies fourth-quarter Adjusted Operating EBITDA 10.54% below the third quarter at the midpoint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-12_exhibit991supplementalsche.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-04_exhibit991supplementalsche.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_exhibit991supplementalsche.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation FC11; calculation FC12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against the favourable view is that earnings quality and cash do not yet match the headline: issuer Adjusted Operating EBITDA exceeds reported EBITDA by USD 216 million over the last twelve months, adjusted free cash flow of USD 607 million is USD 250 million above the free cash flow that creditors actually receive, selling, general and administrative costs grew faster than sales, and guidance implies a fourth quarter below the third. If the next two quarters show lower volume, free cash flow conversion below 31.23% or adjusted items that recur, the view would weaken.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_exhibit991supplementalsche.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation FC1; calculation FC3; calculation FC9; calculation FC11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve with free cash flow conversion back above the FY2025 level of 70.42%, a fourth quarter at or above the third quarter, debt repaid from cash flow and confirmation from the proxy statement and executed debt documents that ownership is dispersed and distributions are capped. It would worsen with a volume loss at Samsung or TSMC, export-control action on China, DuPont settlements beyond the reasonably possible range, or debt-funded shareholder returns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation FC6; calculation FC11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No sector growth data, peer margins or wafer-start trends were supplied, so the finding that volume growth of 21% reflects share gains and content growth and not only an industry upswing rests on management statements and could be wrong if the cycle is turning.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Guidance is a forward-looking management statement and the fourth quarter implied by it is arithmetic, so the finding that guidance implies a pause could be reversed by the first fourth-quarter release.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Comparatives before 2025-11-01 are carve-out statements and the releases use pro forma comparatives, so the incremental margin of 34.51% to 39.67% is a range by basis and the operating-leverage finding could be overstated if stand-alone costs prove higher.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No interest rate hedge, covenant ratio or executed debt terms were supplied, so the finding that refinancing capacity is sound rests on the 2025 issuance and the 2026 repricing and not on lender documents or ratings, and a weaker market could change it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Fixed and variable cost shares, capacity utilization and the maintenance share of capital expenditures are not disclosed, so the downside finding that costs adjust only partly rests on the size of research and administrative spending and on capital expenditures close to depreciation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation FC3; calculation FC8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five strongest credit supports, in order, are these. First, consumable materials qualified into customer roadmaps give recurring volume, which lifted nine-month net sales 20.65% and supports debt service for as long as customers keep producing. Second, margins widened with volume, with gross margin up 0.96 percentage points and an incremental Adjusted Operating EBITDA margin of 34.51%, which lets earnings outgrow debt. Third, leverage is moderate at 2.72x reported EBITDA and liquidity of USD 2,362 million covers twelve-month debt service 9.12x. Fourth, 97.07% of principal falls due in 2032 and 2033, so no refinancing is needed before the revolver matures in October 2030. Fifth, about 70% of raw materials are sourced locally and no supplier exceeds 10% of raw material spend, which limits input and tariff shocks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five largest credit weaknesses, in order, are these. First, the top ten customers took 34% of 2025 sales without purchase commitments and Asia Pacific supplied 78.82%, so one shock hits most volume. Second, free cash flow conversion fell to 31.23% from 53.23% as working capital absorbed USD 134 million, and the reported-to-adjusted EBITDA gap of USD 216 million means cash costs sit outside the adjusted measure. Third, DuPont controls legacy liabilities of USD 218 million that Qnity must fund, with up to about USD 100 million more reasonably possible. Fourth, 57.19% of principal floats and no hedge is disclosed, so each 100 bp costs about USD 24 million a year, and cash paid for interest is not stated in any filing. Fifth, buybacks and dividends took 35.01% of nine-month free cash flow with the limits of the executed documents not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation FC1; calculation FC6; calculation FC7; calculation FC13; calculation FC18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Qnity sells consumable materials that chipmakers and circuit-board makers qualify into their production roadmaps: planarization pads and slurries, photoresists and cleaning chemistries in Semiconductor Technologies, and plating, packaging, thermal and flexible-circuit materials in Interconnect Solutions. Over 90% of 2025 net sales came from products consumed in manufacturing or built into devices, so revenue follows customers' unit output and not one-off projects, which supports cash-flow visibility without giving contractual certainty, because top customers give no long-term purchase commitments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business was part of DuPont until 2025-11-01, so statements for 2025 and earlier are carve-out statements and year-on-year comparisons rely on pro forma measures, and since the separation Qnity carries USD 4,100 million of principal debt that the carve-out did not, which turned an unlevered unit into a leveraged issuer with creditors ranking ahead of equity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; calculation FC14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is public with no sponsor identified, and the credit-relevant structure sits in the separation terms: DuPont holds sole authority over legacy claims that Qnity funds at 44%, one preferred share held by a trust can block charter changes that protect that authority, and the sponsor and governance risk level is Medium. For creditors this means no sponsor exit pressure or fee leakage, but a perpetual outflow risk that the board cannot contest, and shareholder returns of 35.01% of nine-month free cash flow with the capacity limits of the executed documents not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue growth is volume, not price: nine-month net sales rose 20.65% on volume of 21% with local price and mix flat, against volume of 11% and price and mix of minus 1% in 2025 and volume of 10% and price and mix of minus 2% in 2024. Management attributes demand to artificial intelligence, advanced nodes and packaging that raise material content per wafer, and Interconnect Solutions volume rose 27% against 16% in Semiconductor Technologies, so Interconnect Solutions supplied 69.34% of the growth in segment Adjusted Operating EBITDA. The mechanism is repeat consumption qualified into customer roadmaps, which supports volume but gives Qnity little pricing power, so earnings follow customers' output and creditors should expect them to fall when output does.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation FC4; calculation FC5; calculation FC19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is rising: Samsung took 12% of net sales in 2023 and 10% in the nine months of 2026, TSMC rose from 6% to 10%, and the top ten customers took 32% in 2023 and 34% in 2025. Contracts carry no long-term purchase commitments and orders can be cancelled, so a decision at either customer moves a tenth of sales at once.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are widening but the cost base is semi-fixed: cost of sales fell to 53% of net sales and gross margin rose to 47.14% from 46.18%, yet research and development plus selling, general and administrative costs of USD 870 million are 20.23% of net sales and selling, general and administrative costs grew 26.49% against sales growth of 20.65%. The split between fixed and variable cost is not disclosed, so operating leverage is read from the incremental margin of 34.51%, which implies that a volume decline would take back margin at a similar rate. Metals pass-through and local sourcing limit input shocks, which supports margin stability in a normal year but not in a volume shock.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation FC2; calculation FC3; calculation FC4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is rising and conversion has dropped: capital expenditures of USD 290 million equal 98.98% of depreciation and amortization and 6.74% of net sales, free cash flow was 31.23% of reported EBITDA against 53.23% a year earlier, and working capital absorbed USD 134 million, 18.21% of the increase in net sales. Interest expense reached USD 186 million in nine months because the separation debt was raised in 2025, and the issuer's adjusted free cash flow of USD 607 million adds back USD 250 million of transformation, legacy and tax costs that remain cash costs for creditors. Capital expenditures close to depreciation limit the cash that spending cuts could release in a downturn, although working capital would release cash if volume fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_exhibit991supplementalsche.htm.jsonl, page 11; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation FC6; calculation FC7; calculation FC8; calculation FC9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is moderate: the named rivals are Entegris, Merck KGA, Resonac, Element Solutions and MKS Instruments, competition is on performance, quality and reliability, and price and mix of minus 1% in 2025 and minus 2% in 2024 show some price give, yet an adjusted EBITDA margin of 30.87% shows Qnity holds its position. The threat of new entrants is low because qualification cycles run for several quarters and customers qualify materials into node roadmaps, which protects the volume base. The threat of substitutes is moderate because node, chiplet and packaging changes can re-specify materials, and failure to keep pace would cost share. Buyer power is high, with the top ten customers at 34% of sales and no purchase commitments. Supplier power is low, with about 70% of raw materials sourced locally and no supplier above 10% of raw material spend, which limits input-cost shocks and supports margin stability.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 67; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation FC1; calculation FC19; calculation FC20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors are material because trade restrictions, export controls on technology to China and tariffs can cut demand or competitiveness, and China supplied 33.02% of 2025 net sales; the filings also name the Middle East conflict as a supply and energy risk that has not yet had a material effect. Economic factors are material because customers' capital spending and inventory cycles set volume, and technological factors are material because artificial intelligence and advanced packaging drive content growth. Social factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.

fields.value: - Opportunity: content growth from advanced packaging and artificial intelligence could keep volume above customers' output growth, and guidance raised at each release shows momentum.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Threat: export controls, tariffs or inventory corrections at Samsung or TSMC could reduce volume at once, and a rise of 100 bp in rates adds about USD 24 million of annual interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are scale, a 30.87% adjusted EBITDA margin, moderate leverage, large liquidity and a distant maturity wall; the constraints are customer and regional concentration, cash conversion, DuPont-controlled liabilities and a floating-rate term loan. The trend is improving on earnings, with total leverage down to 2.72x from 2.87x since 2025-12-31 and net leverage down to 1.96x from 2.22x, but not yet on cash; pro forma net leverage after the dividend declared on 2026-10-14 is not established. Key missing datapoints are cash paid for interest, the first lien net leverage ratio, hedging terms, and revenue by product line.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation FC1; calculation FC6; calculation FC13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are guidance raised at each release to net sales of USD 5,770 million to USD 5,830 million, growth of 22.00% at the midpoint, and content growth from advanced packaging; the headwinds are an implied fourth quarter 3.60% below the third in net sales and 10.54% below in Adjusted Operating EBITDA at the midpoints, the cash costs of the transformation plan and legacy settlements, and a seasonal pattern that peaks in the second and third quarters. The implied fourth quarter is still above the fourth quarter of 2025, so the pause reads as seasonality or caution and not a downturn, which the next release will test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; EX-99.1_2026-05-12_exhibit991supplementalsche.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-04_exhibit991supplementalsche.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_exhibit991supplementalsche.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation FC10; calculation FC11; calculation FC12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the debt is back-ended: 97.07% of principal falls due in 2032 and 2033, the notes become callable at specified prices from 2028-08-15, and the revolver matures in October 2030. The medium-term risk is therefore less liquidity than the cost and availability of refinancing USD 4,100 million of principal at the time, with 57.19% floating until then, and the DuPont cost-sharing arrangement that runs to 2040-12-31 at the latest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2025-12-31_q-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation FC13; calculation FC14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside starts with an export-control or tariff action, or an inventory correction at a top customer, that cuts Asia Pacific volume, which is 78.82% of sales. The first operational break is order cancellation, because contracts carry no purchase commitments, and price and mix history of minus 1% and minus 2% shows little price offset. Margin then falls because research and administrative costs of USD 870 million are semi-fixed and the incremental margin of 34.51% works in reverse. Free cash flow is cushioned because receivables and inventories that absorbed USD 134 million would release, but legacy payments, dividends and buybacks continue unless management cuts them, and capital expenditures close to depreciation leave limited room to cut.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation FC3; calculation FC4; calculation FC7; calculation FC8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On leverage, total debt to reported EBITDA returns to its 2025-12-31 level of 2.87x if last-twelve-month EBITDA falls 5.32% and net debt to reported EBITDA returns to 2.22x if it falls 11.83%, with pro forma net leverage after the dividend declared on 2026-10-14 not established. Liquidity of USD 2,362 million still covers twelve-month debt service of principal and interest 9.12x and no maturity falls before 2030, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; the weak point is leverage drifting back up while a floating-rate term loan reprices, and buybacks, USD 75 million in nine months, are the first lever to pull.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_q-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation FC1; calculation FC13; calculation FC16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Qnity presents a strong business profile supported by consumable, roadmap-qualified products, volume-led growth and a 30.87% adjusted EBITDA margin, but credit quality is constrained by customer and regional concentration, a drop in cash conversion to 31.23% of reported EBITDA and DuPont-controlled legacy liabilities of USD 218 million. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because liquidity of USD 2,362 million and 2.72x total leverage cushion a volume shock, although conversion has not yet followed earnings. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings holding through 2032 and 2033, when 97.07% of principal falls due, and on rates for the 57.19% that floats. The primary downside path is an export-control, tariff or inventory shock in Asia Pacific that cancels orders and deleverages semi-fixed costs. Further analysis would require cash paid for interest, the covenant ratio and executed debt terms, hedging terms, revenue by product line and sector data.
